evals.prompt: Audit this repo for loop engineering readiness. It's a Rails 7.1 app. Root contains: Gemfile, Gemfile.lock, .ruby-version, README.md, bin/setup, bin/rails, bin/rubocop, spec/ with ~300 specs, .github/workflows/ci.yml running `bundle exec rspec` and `bundle exec rubocop`, docker-compose.yml with postgres. There is no AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md. README says `bin/setup` then `bin/rails s`. Running `bundle exec rspec` took 3m10s and exited 0.
evals.expected_output: Verdict Not ready with one blocker: no agent instructions file (dimension 1, check 1.1). Environment, verification and CI dimensions mostly Ready. Work Plan item 1 is adding AGENTS.md (effort S) starting from the starter asset; report printed in full and saved to docs/loop-engineering-audit.md.
expectations: Response grades the missing AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md as a 🔴 Blocker under dimension 1 and the overall verdict is Not ready
Response's Work Plan lists creating AGENTS.md as task #1 with effort S
Response grades the test command 🟢 on runtime (3m10s is under the 5-minute default budget) rather than flagging it
Response does not invent blockers for dimensions 2, 3, or 6 given the pinned Ruby version, committed lockfile, bin/setup, and CI running the same commands
Response states the report is printed in chat and saved to docs/loop-engineering-audit.md without committing it

evals.prompt: Can AI agents work on this project autonomously? It's a Node/TypeScript service. package.json scripts: {"dev": "tsx watch src/index.ts", "test": "jest --watch", "lint": "eslint ."}. There's a tsconfig.json but no typecheck script. CLAUDE.md exists and says: 'Run npm test before committing.' No lockfile is committed (.gitignore has package-lock.json). CI: none.
evals.expected_output: Not ready. Blockers: `npm test` is watch-mode only (3.3) and CLAUDE.md documents it as the command (1.3/1.6); lockfile ignored (2.2); no CI (6.1). Gap: no typecheck script (3.1). Work Plan orders: fix test script to `jest --ci`, commit lockfile, add typecheck, add CI, update CLAUDE.md.
expectations: Response identifies `jest --watch` as a 🔴 Blocker because it never exits in an unattended loop, and proposes `jest --ci` (or CI=1) as the fix
Response flags that CLAUDE.md points agents at the watch-mode command, so the documented command is wrong, not just missing
Response grades the ignored package-lock.json as a 🔴 Blocker under reproducible environment
Response grades missing CI as a 🔴 Blocker under CI & merge gates
Response flags the missing typecheck script as a 🟡 Gap with a concrete fix such as adding "typecheck": "tsc --noEmit"
Response's Work Plan puts blockers before the typecheck gap

evals.prompt: Audit this monorepo for agent readiness. pnpm workspace with apps/web (Next.js) and packages/api (Fastify). Root has AGENTS.md listing `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test` (all defined via turbo.json and each runs non-interactively). .nvmrc, pnpm-lock.yaml, .env.example present. CI runs the three commands on PRs. `gh api` for branch protection returned HTTP 403. There's a bin/reset-db script that drops and recreates the database, not mentioned anywhere. No .claude/settings.json.
evals.expected_output: Partially ready or Ready depending on gaps; no blockers. Branch protection is ⚪ with the question to ask, never guessed. bin/reset-db is a 🟡 guardrail gap (unfenced destructive command) — the audit must not run it. Missing permissions config is a 🟡 at most.
expectations: Response reports no 🔴 Blockers and the verdict is not 'Not ready'
Response lists branch protection as ⚪ Unverifiable with an explicit question for a human, and does not grade it 🟢 or 🔴
Response flags bin/reset-db as a 🟡 guardrails gap because it is destructive, undocumented, and unfenced, and recommends listing it under a 'never run' section of AGENTS.md
Response does not execute bin/reset-db or any setup/migration command
Response treats the absent .claude/settings.json permissions as a 🟡 or informational item, not a blocker

evals.prompt: Re-run the loop engineering audit on this Python project. .eagerworks/loop-engineering-audit.json contains {"dimensions": {"taskDefinition": {"enabled": false}}, "budgets": {"testSeconds": 60}}. pyproject.toml with uv.lock, .python-version, ruff and pytest configured, AGENTS.md accurate. `pytest -q` ran in 2m05s, exit 0. No CI. A previous docs/loop-engineering-audit.md exists from last month.
evals.expected_output: Dimension 5 is excluded and disclosed in the footer; 2m05s exceeds the configured 60 s budget so 3.5 is 🟡; no CI is 🔴 so verdict Not ready. The existing report is overwritten, not appended, and a 'Since last audit' note is included.
expectations: Response excludes dimension 5 (task definition) from the scorecard and explicitly discloses that it was disabled by config
Response grades the 2m05s test runtime as 🟡 because the configured budget is 60 seconds, not the 5-minute default
Response grades missing CI as 🔴 and the verdict is Not ready
Response overwrites docs/loop-engineering-audit.md rather than creating a dated or numbered second file
Response mentions comparing against the previous audit (a 'Since last audit' section) without skipping any checks

evals.prompt: What's missing for Claude Code to work on this repo in a loop? Rails app. AGENTS.md documents `bin/test` and `bin/lint`. bin/ contains rails, rake, setup, rubocop — there is no bin/test or bin/lint. spec/ has 40 files; `grep -rL 'expect' spec/` lists 12 of them. expectations: Response grades the non-existent bin/test and bin/lint referenced in AGENTS.md as a 🔴 Blocker, citing that documented commands must exist on disk
Response's Work Plan #1 is either adding bin/test and bin/lint wrappers or correcting AGENTS.md to the real commands
Response flags the 12 assertion-free spec files as a 🟡 Gap under test coverage with the grep as evidence
Response notes the divergence between documented commands and what CI runs
Response does not claim dimension 2 (environment) has problems given the committed lockfile and .ruby-version

AGENTS.md is complete and accurate (`pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test` = `vitest run`, runtimes listed, conventions and a never-run list). pnpm-lock.yaml, .nvmrc, no env vars needed. 180 tests, c8 coverage at 85% threshold, vitest run took 40s. Response's Work Plan is empty or explicitly states there is no required work, and does not add style preferences to look thorough
